raw_case_text: The second patient was a 17-year-old girl without family history of TB. She presented with numerous bilateral cervical lymphadenopathies and nasal obstruction. Nasal endoscopy found a polypoid uprising of the superior and posterior nasopharyngeal walls. CT scan showed a nasopharyngeal mass with central hypodensity suggesting tissue necrosis (Figure 3), with multiple cervical lymphadenopathies. A biopsy was performed.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 17-year-old female presented with nasal obstruction and bilateral neck swelling.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with nasal obstruction and numerous bilateral cervical swellings.
subjective.review_of_systems: Patient reported nasal obstruction. Systemic symptoms, home medications, and allergies: unmentioned.

objective.physical_examination: Presence of numerous bilateral cervical lymphadenopathies.
objective.advanced_workup: Nasal endoscopy: revealed polypoid swelling and mucosal uprising of the superior and posterior nasopharyngeal walls. CT scan: demonstrated a nasopharyngeal mass with central hypodensity suggestive of tissue necrosis, accompanied by multiple cervical lymphadenopathies. Nasopharyngeal biopsy was performed.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Primary nasopharyngeal tuberculosis presenting with central necrosis mimicking nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Diagnostic biopsy was performed; across this patient series, histopathology confirmed granulomatous nasopharyngitis with epithelioid histiocytes, Langhans multinucleated giant cells, and caseous necrosis. Managed with antitubercular regimen comprising rifampicin (10 mg/kg/day), isoniazid (5 mg/kg/day), and pyrazinamide (20 mg/kg/day) for 2 months, followed by rifampicin and isoniazid for 4 months, achieving favorable clinical and radiological resolution.
